claim: GitHub's security-features page lists push protection as enabled by default and free on public repositories. The push-protection page separately says the repository-level setting is off by default and is turned on by a repository admin under Settings, Security and quality, Advanced Security, then Secret Protection and Push protection. The two statements may refer to different layers (account-level versus repository-level), so the owner must confirm in the Settings page that repository-level push protection shows as enabled. Anyone with write access can bypass a block by giving a reason (used in tests, false positive, or fix later), and delegated bypass can limit who may do so.

source.locator: steps to enable; also about-push-protection page and github-security-features page
